audit_scope.description: Files describe EL-specific components including BLAKE2b precompile execution, SSTORE gas metering, EVM storage operations, block reward calculations, difficulty adjustments, and EIP-7594 blob transaction validation. These are all Execution Layer concerns except for EIP-7594 which bridges CL data availability with EL transaction processing.

in_scope: SSTORE opcode gas metering and state transitions
Storage slot state transitions within transactions
Gas refund mechanisms for storage operations
EVM execution context and call frames
out_of_scope: EIP editor governance (meta-process, no runtime impact)
Peer discovery protocols (P2P layer implementation details)
Cryptographic primitive internals (BLAKE2, KZG proofs assumed correct)

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.description: External users or applications submitting blob transactions (EIP-4844/EIP-7594) through the P2P gossip network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction submitters are anonymous, unauthenticated network participants. They can submit arbitrary transaction payloads, including malformed blobs, invalid KZG commitments, incorrect cell proofs, or transactions designed to exploit validation logic. All inputs must be fully validated.
data_flows: Blob data (up to 6 blobs per transaction)
Cell proofs for data availability sampling
threat_profile: Malformed transaction data to trigger validation bypass
Invalid KZG proofs to pass without proper blob data
Excessive blob counts (>6) to cause resource exhaustion
Mismatched quantities (hashes vs blobs vs commitments) to trigger logic errors
Crafted cell proofs to fake data availability

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Creator via RPC/Wallet
trusted_external_entities.description: End users creating and submitting blob transactions through wallets or RPC interfaces
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users can be malicious or compromised. They control transaction content, gas parameters, blob data, and can attempt to exploit transaction validation or processing logic. No assumption of benign behavior can be made.
data_flows: Transaction parameters (to, from, value, gas, data)
threat_profile: Malicious transaction payloads targeting smart contract vulnerabilities
Gas manipulation to cause resource exhaustion
Invalid blob wrapper formats to bypass validation
Replay attacks using old transaction signatures

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Network Nodes (DAS Sampling)
trusted_external_entities.description: Remote P2P nodes that custody blob column data and respond to data availability sampling requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes are anonymous, potentially Byzantine actors. They may withhold data, provide incorrect column data, send invalid KZG proofs, or collude to perform data withholding attacks. The PeerDAS security model assumes an honest majority but individual peers cannot be trusted.
threat_profile: Data withholding attacks (refusing to provide columns)
Invalid column data with forged proofs
Sybil attacks to control column custody distribution
DoS via excessive sampling requests or slow responses
Eclipse attacks to isolate nodes from honest peers

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Column Custodians (Reconstruction)
trusted_external_entities.description: Peer nodes that maintain custody of specific columns for data reconstruction when <50% columns initially available
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Same as EXT-PEER-NODES. These are untrusted peers that may withhold missing columns to prevent reconstruction, especially in coordinated data withholding attacks.
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P request-response protocol for missing column requests
threat_profile: Coordinated withholding of critical columns to prevent reconstruction
Invalid data responses during reconstruction attempts
Timing attacks (delaying responses to cause timeouts)

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Propagation Peer Nodes
trusted_external_entities.description: Remote P2P nodes propagating newly produced blocks through the network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers can propagate invalid blocks with incorrect difficulty calculations, wrong reward amounts, or manipulated state roots. They may be Byzantine actors attempting to cause chain splits or fork the network. All received blocks must be fully validated.
threat_profile: Invalid difficulty values to bypass difficulty bomb delay
Incorrect reward calculations to inflate supply or steal rewards
Malformed block headers to trigger parsing vulnerabilities
Uncle spam to manipulate nephew rewards
Chain reorganization attacks with withheld blocks

boundary_edges.description: Blob transaction with wrapper enters EL validation pipeline from untrusted P2P gossip
validation_required: Equal quantities of versioned hashes, blobs, commitments
KZG commitments hash to versioned hashes
Batch verification of all cell proofs

boundary_edges.description: User-created blob transaction enters EL mempool via RPC interface
validation_required: Gas price and gas limit validation

boundary_edges.description: Column samples from untrusted peers enter DAS verification process
validation_required: KZG proof verification for each column
Sufficient diversity of column sources (>50% for reconstruction)

boundary_edges.description: Missing column data provided by peers for erasure code reconstruction
Block propagated from peer node enters validation pipeline
validation_required: Difficulty matches expected calculation (with fake_block_number if post-Constantinople)
Block reward correctly calculated (2 ETH post-Constantinople, 3 ETH pre)
State root consistency with applied transactions and rewards

notes: All truly external entities have been identified and mapped to boundary edges
Several entities were correctly identified as misclassified internal components
EIP-5069 governance entities excluded as out-of-scope (meta-process, no protocol runtime)
EIP-7594 (PeerDAS) introduces multiple untrusted P2P boundaries for blob data availability
All trust levels are UNTRUSTED as these are public, unauthenticated network interfaces
EIP-2200 and EIP-1234 validation logic is entirely internal after initial block/transaction receipt
